title: Does AI-driven productivity come at the cost of code quality?
summary: Short clip claiming AI gives a temporary productivity bump that turns into technical debt, and that engineers must learn when to use AI and when not to.

assertions.quote: there is a temporary increase usually across most companies right in productivity thing for the first couple of months.

verdicts.note: A difference-in-differences study of Cursor adoption found transient velocity gains with lasting complexity increases, but other field data show sustained gains.

Second-hand only: cites He et al., where Cursor adoption in 807 repos gave a transient velocity boost but persistent increases in code complexity. That fits the claim, but the paper does not itself measure productivity.

The review notes that several sources warn short-term gains may come at the expense of long-term maintainability, but it states that longitudinal evidence is limited and that long-horizon outcomes are rarely examined, so it cannot tell whether gains fade.

assertions.quote: it creates technical debt and a decrease in code quality which then means that for the subsequent months your productivity slows down
for the first two months you might perceive that you're moving faster but in reality
the limitation is always evolving and changing
